name: nonApi_checkReminders
description: Timer-triggered SP (RunCheckInNotification, every 1 minute) that scans HC.Event for events within the check-in reminder window (±11 minutes from start) or RSVP reminder window (±3 days from start) that have not yet had their reminder sent. Returns two rowsets consumed by the C# timer trigger to dispatch FCM pushes, then stamps CheckInReminderSent / RsvpReminderSent on HC.Event so reminders are not re-sent on the next tick. No parameters — called inside Azure Functions and not publicly accessible.

rowsets.name: MessageDetails
rowsets.description: One row per qualifying event (minutesToEvent > 0). Empty when no reminders are due. Consumed by the C# RunCheckInNotification trigger to build FCM notification payloads. MessageRelesabilityFlags column name preserves the HC5 typo so the C# EventMessage deserialiser continues to work without a breaking change.

columns.name: MessageId
columns.description: NEWID() generated per qualifying event — shared key between Rowset 0 and Rowset 1.

columns.name: PublicEventId
columns.description: HC.Event.PublicEventId — public-facing event UUID for deep-links in push notifications.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: PublicHasherId of the HC system user ('B6BAFD0D-5D2E-41CD-8495-811D551F01D0'). Always the same hardcoded system user.

columns.name: UserDisplayName
columns.description: HC.Hasher.DisplayName for the HC system user. Computed column from Hasher table.

columns.name: UserPhoto
columns.description: HC.Hasher.Photo for the HC system user. Table column is NVARCHAR(1000) NULL.

columns.name: MessageTitle
columns.description: Notification title: 'Time to check in' (MessageType=1) or 'Time to RSVP' (MessageType=2).

columns.name: MessageContent
columns.description: Notification body text constructed from event name and time-to-event. Human-readable string with time units (minutes/hours/days).

columns.name: MessageRelesabilityFlags
columns.description: Always 65535. Intentional typo in column name ('Relesability' not 'Releasability') preserved for C# EventMessage deserialiser compatibility.

columns.name: EventChatMessageCount
columns.description: Always 0. Obsolete since app version 2.1.3; kept for C# deserialiser compatibility.

columns.name: MessageType
columns.description: 1 = check-in reminder (within ±11 minutes of event start), 2 = RSVP reminder (within ±3 days of event start).

rowsets.name: Recipients
rowsets.description: One row per FCM token that should receive the push for a given event. For MessageType=1 (check-in): filtered to tokens within 100 km of the event and not already checked in. For MessageType=2 (RSVP): all token holders who have not yet RSVPd. May be empty when no qualifying recipients exist.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: HC.HasherKennelMap.UserId — the recipient hasher's internal UUID.

columns.name: FcmToken
columns.description: HC.Device.FcmToken — the FCM registration token for this device. May be NULL (for check-in pushes, geo-filter may pass NULL-token devices if GeoPoint matches; for RSVP pushes, NULL tokens are explicitly excluded).

columns.name: EventId
columns.description: The event this push relates to — links back to Rowset 0 EventId.

columns.name: MessageId
columns.description: NEWID() from #messages — links back to Rowset 0 MessageId.

sideEffects: Stamps HC.Event.CheckInReminderSent = GETDATE() for all type-1 events returned in Rowset 0.
Stamps HC.Event.RsvpReminderSent = GETDATE() for all type-2 events returned in Rowset 0.
On stamp failure: inserts an error row into HC.ErrorLog (does not abort — rowsets have already been returned).
Stamp failures cause the reminder to be re-sent on the next timer tick (preferred over silent failure).

codeSmells.issue: Rowsets are returned before the stamp UPDATE commits
codeSmells.detail: Steps 3 and 4 SELECT from #messages and return the rowsets, then Step 5 issues the UPDATE inside TRY/CATCH. If the timer trigger reads the rowsets and dispatches pushes before the stamp completes, and the stamp then fails, the next timer tick will re-process the same events and send duplicate reminders. This is documented as the preferred trade-off (duplicate reminder vs. lost push), but callers must be aware of the idempotency risk.

codeSmells.issue: Check-in recipient filter can return rows with NULL FcmToken
codeSmells.detail: The check-in (MessageType=1) UNION branch filters d.Latitude IS NOT NULL and uses GeoPoint.STDistance for geo-fencing but does not filter d.FcmToken IS NOT NULL. Recipients with a known location but a NULL FCM token will appear in Rowset 1. The C# caller must guard against null tokens before dispatching.

The HC system user id ('0CDBB109-215E-4B5F-A405-F6C9FBCB18EC') and PublicHasherId ('B6BAFD0D-5D2E-41CD-8495-811D551F01D0') are hardcoded literals. If these ever change in the DB, the SP breaks silently.

codeSmells.issue: No TRY/CATCH around main SELECT steps
codeSmells.detail: Only Step 5 (the stamp UPDATE) is wrapped in TRY/CATCH. An unexpected error in Steps 1-4 (the #temp population or SELECT queries) will propagate as a raw SQL exception to the C# timer trigger with no structured error rowset.
Column alias 'MessageRelesabilityFlags' (misspelling of 'Releasability') is intentionally preserved to avoid a C# breaking change. This is a known documented smell, not an accidental bug.

breakingChanges: HC5 accepted an @apiKey parameter and validated it against a hardcoded key. HC6 removes @apiKey entirely — the timer trigger is internal to Azure Functions.
HC5 wrote a startup entry to LOG.GeneralLog. HC6 removes this noise (timer runs every minute).
HC5 stamp failure caused the SP to abort with a raw error. HC6 wraps the stamp in TRY/CATCH and continues — duplicate reminders are possible on transient stamp failures.
